section_name: In-Sample Residual Correction vs. Held-Out Evaluation

candidates.title: How Biased Is the Apparent Error Rate of a Prediction Rule?
candidates.reason: Establishes the foundational distinction between evaluating a rule on the observations used to fit it ('apparent error') versus independent test data, proving that in-sample evaluation is inherently optimistic because the data are used twice.

candidates.title: The Estimation of Prediction Error: Covariance Penalties and Cross-Validation
candidates.reason: Quantifies the mathematical optimism penalty separating in-sample residual error from expected out-of-sample prediction error, showing why zeroing residual error on the estimation sample does not imply generalization.

candidates.title: Cross-Validatory Choice and Assessment of Statistical Predictions
candidates.reason: Seminal paper demonstrating that predictive assessment is invalid when conducted on the calibration sample, establishing held-out cross-validation as necessary to determine whether a rule transfers beyond its estimation data.

candidates.title: The Predictive Sample Reuse Method with Applications
candidates.reason: Formalizes predictive sample reuse and held-out validation to separate descriptive sample-fitting from genuine predictive capability on unseen targets.

candidates.title: Stacked Generalization
candidates.reason: Demonstrates that learning corrections or combining models on raw in-sample errors produces severe overfitting and trivial memorization, establishing data partitioning as essential for residual-based adjustments.

candidates.title: Stacked Regressions
candidates.reason: Analyzes post-hoc linear corrections and model blending, proving that estimating adjustment parameters on in-sample residuals yields artificially reduced errors that do not reflect out-of-sample performance.

candidates.title: Probabilistic Outputs for Support Vector Machines and Comparisons to Regularized Likelihood Methods
candidates.reason: Analyzes post-hoc scalar adjustments (Platt scaling) and explicitly shows that fitting scalar calibration parameters on estimation data leads to extreme in-sample optimism, requiring separate held-out validation.

candidates.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
candidates.reason: Investigates scalar post-hoc adjustment (temperature scaling) and shows that even single-parameter corrections must be evaluated on distinct held-out data to assess whether the correction genuinely transfers.

candidates.title: Double/Debiased Machine Learning for Treatment and Structural Parameters
candidates.reason: Demonstrates that residual evaluation on the same observations used for estimation induces mechanical own-observation bias, establishing cross-fitting as mandatory for valid out-of-sample residual behavior.

candidates.title: Distribution-Free Predictive Inference for Regression
candidates.reason: Proves that residual-based scalar corrections and predictive intervals require held-out calibration splits to guarantee valid predictive coverage on unseen inputs rather than trivial in-sample fit.

candidates.title: Cross-Validation: What Does It Estimate and How Well Does It Do It?
candidates.reason: Clarifies the precise scope of sample-based error estimates, demonstrating why calculations on a fixed finite sample describe only that specific sample rather than out-of-sample predictive performance.

candidates.title: Leakage and the Reproducibility Crisis in Machine-Learning-Based Science
candidates.reason: Examines data leakage where adjustment parameters are evaluated on the data used to calculate them, showing how this produces illusory performance gains that do not transfer to independent test sets.

candidates.title: Some Comments on Cp
candidates.reason: Shows that minimizing or nullifying in-sample residual sum of squares is a mathematical consequence of fitting rather than an indicator of low expected prediction error on new observations.
